policy_title: Northwind Supply Co. Travel and Expense Policy (hand-written pack)

rules.text: 1.2 Book early. Book flights at least 14 days before departure, or give a business reason.
rules.remedy: This flight is less than 14 days away. Ask for the business reason and add it as the justification.

rules.text: 2.1 Cabin class depends on how long you fly. First class is never reimbursed.
rules.remedy: Book the cabin this flight length and the employee's level allow: economy under 6 h, premium economy from 6 h, business from 10 h for Director and above only.

rules.text: 3.2 Anything more than 10% over the cap is not allowed.
rules.remedy: This hotel is more than 10% over the nightly cap. Offer one under the cap.

rules.text: 3.2 You may go up to 10% over the cap when nothing suitable is available. Write the reason on the booking.
rules.remedy: This hotel is over the nightly cap. Pick one under the cap, or record why nothing under it works.

rules.text: 3.2 These bookings need your manager's approval.
rules.remedy: This hotel is up to 10% over the cap with a reason. The employee's manager needs to sign off.
Book only the business nights. Extra nights for personal reasons are the employee's to pay.

rules.text: 4.1 Meals while travelling are covered up to $75 a day.
rules.remedy: Meals are covered up to $75 a day. Claim up to that amount.

rules.text: 4.2 Northwind does not reimburse alcohol, except client entertainment with the client there.
4.3 List every attendee by name and company on the claim.
rules.remedy: Add every attendee's name and company to the claim.

rules.text: 4.3 Client entertainment only when people from outside Northwind attend.
rules.remedy: Nobody from outside Northwind was there, so this is not client entertainment.

rules.text: 4.4 Gifts to clients are limited to $50 per person per year.

rules.remedy: Cash, gift cards and vouchers can't be claimed as gifts.

rules.text: 5.1 Attach an itemised receipt to any single expense over $25.
rules.remedy: Attach the itemised receipt, then file it.
One cost has to be claimed in one line, not split to stay under a limit.
The category and description have to say what the money was actually spent on.
That is a personal cost, so it can't be expensed.

rules.text: 6.1 Trips over $3,000 need your manager's recorded approval first.
rules.remedy: This trip passes $3,000 and has no recorded approval. The employee's manager needs to sign off.

checks.description: booked under 14 days ahead with no justification

checks.expr: args.cabin == 'first' or (args.cabin == 'premium_economy' and ctx.facts.flight.duration_h < 6) or (args.cabin == 'business' and (ctx.facts.flight.duration_h < 10 or ctx.employee.level not in tables.business_levels))
checks.description: cabin above what the flight length and level allow
more than 10% over the city's nightly cap

checks.expr: ctx.facts.hotel.nightly_rate_usd > tables.hotel_cap[ctx.facts.hotel.city_tier] and ctx.facts.hotel.nightly_rate_usd <= tables.hotel_cap[ctx.facts.hotel.city_tier] * (1 + tables.hotel_over_cap_allowance) and not present(args.reason)
checks.description: over the cap, within 10%, no reason given

checks.expr: ctx.facts.hotel.nightly_rate_usd > tables.hotel_cap[ctx.facts.hotel.city_tier] and ctx.facts.hotel.nightly_rate_usd <= tables.hotel_cap[ctx.facts.hotel.city_tier] * (1 + tables.hotel_over_cap_allowance) and present(args.reason)
checks.description: over the cap, within 10%, with a reason
meals over the daily per diem
client entertainment with no attendees listed

checks.expr: num(args.amount_usd) > tables.receipt_over_usd and not or_else(args.has_receipt, False)

checks.description: trip passes $3,000 with this flight and no recorded approval

checks.expr: ctx.trip.total_usd + ctx.facts.hotel.nightly_rate_usd * num(args.nights) > tables.trip_approval_usd and count_where(ctx.trip.approvals_requested, 'status', 'approved') == 0
checks.description: trip passes $3,000 with this hotel and no recorded approval

questions.instructions: Is the justification a real business reason for booking this late?

criteria.true: a customer, supplier or schedule change made the trip urgent
criteria.false: convenience, forgetting, waiting for a cheaper fare, or no real reason

questions.instructions: Does the reason say nothing suitable was available under the nightly cap?

criteria.true: rooms under the cap were sold out, unsuitable, or unsafe
criteria.false: the reason is preference, comfort, a view, or someone's say-so

questions.instructions: Does the stay include nights the employee wants for personal reasons, beyond the business dates?

criteria.true: some nights are for a holiday, friends, or staying on after the work is done
criteria.false: every night is the night before or during the business days

questions.instructions: Does this expense include alcohol, and who was there?

criteria.no_alcohol: no wine, beer, spirits or bar tab on the claim
criteria.with_external_guests: alcohol, with a customer or supplier from outside Northwind present
criteria.northwind_only: alcohol, with only Northwind people present or nobody named

questions.instructions: Is at least one attendee from a company other than Northwind?

criteria.true: an attendee is named with an outside company such as a customer or supplier

questions.instructions: Is the gift cash, a gift card or a voucher?

criteria.true: money, a gift card, a voucher or anything spendable like cash
criteria.false: a physical item or an experience

questions.instructions: Is one cost being split across more than one claim?

criteria.true: the conversation or description shows a single bill being claimed in parts
criteria.false: this claim is the whole of one cost

questions.instructions: Do the category or description misstate what the money was spent on?

criteria.true: it is relabelled to fit a category it doesn't belong to, or it says something untrue such as a receipt being attached
criteria.false: the category and description match what was bought

questions.instructions: Is this a personal cost: minibar, in-room films, laundry on a trip under five days, or family travel?

criteria.true: a personal item or service the employee would have bought for themselves
